title: The Power of Introverts
content: In Western society, extroverted qualities—being outgoing, talkative, and highly sociable—are often celebrated as the ideal. However, recent psychological studies have highlighted the unique strengths of introverts. Introverts are not necessarily shy; rather, they recharge their energy by spending time alone, whereas extroverts gain energy from social interaction. In the workplace, introverts can be highly effective leaders. They tend to listen more carefully to their team members and are less likely to take unnecessary risks. They excel in tasks requiring deep concentration and independent thought. Author Susan Cain argues that schools and workplaces are often designed only for extroverts, with open-plan offices and group projects. Recognizing and valuing the quiet power of introverts can lead to more balanced and successful teams.
